item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The results of a long jump competition were reported as follows:

| | Average Length |
| --- | --- |
| Team A | 3.6 m |
| Team B | 4.8 m |

There were the same number of students in each team.
Which statement about the competition MUST be true?

options.label: A
options.text: Each student in team B jumped farther than any student in team A.

options.label: B
options.text: After every student in team A jumped, there was a student in team B who jumped farther.

options.label: C
options.text: As a group, team B jumped farther than team A.

options.label: D
options.text: Some students in team A jumped farther than some students in team B.

reference_items.stem:
Popularity of Subjects

A group of 10 students wanted to find out whether mathematics or history was more popular for their group. They rated each subject using the following scale.

[Image: Rating scale from 1 to 5]

The table shows the results:

Students’ Ratings

| Student | Mathematics Rating | History Rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alan | 1 | 2 |
| Lisa | 4 | 4 |
| Ann | 5 | 4 |
| John | 2 | 2 |
| Connor | 4 | 2 |
| Georgia | 3 | 3 |
| Bret | 2 | 1 |
| Courtney | 1 | 1 |
| Ian | 5 | 3 |
| Jackson | 3 | 2 |
| Totals | 30 | 24 |

B. The students’ ratings are shown on the graph below. For example, Alan’s name is by his ratings (mathematics 1, history 2).

[Image: Scatter plot showing students' ratings]

Write True or False in the space after each of these statements:

All students in the group liked mathematics more than they liked history. ____

Nearly half of the students gave both subjects the same rating. ____

Two students neither liked nor disliked either subject. ____

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Two-thirds of the people present at the beginning of a meeting are men. Nobody leaves but 10 more men and 10 more women arrive at the meeting. Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: There would then be more men than women at the meeting.

options.label: B
options.text: There would then be the same number of men as there are women at the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: There would then be more women than men at the meeting.

options.label: D
options.text: From the information given, you cannot tell whether there would be more women or men.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jo has three metal blocks. The weight of each block is the same.
When she weighed one block against 8 grams, this is what happened.

[Image: The block is lighter than the weight of 8 grams on the scale.]

When she weighed all three blocks against 20 grams, this is what happened.

[Image: The three blocks are heavier than the weight of 20 grams on the scale.]

Which of the following could be the weight of one metal block?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two balance scale diagrams:
- Top balance scale: The beam is tilted down to the right. On the higher left pan rests one gray rectangular metal block. On the lower right pan rest four weights: one large weight labeled "5g" and three small weights stacked beside it, each labeled "1g" (total 8 grams).
- Bottom balance scale: The beam is tilted down to the left. On the lower left pan rests a stack of three identical gray rectangular metal blocks. On the higher right pan rest two large weights, each labeled "10g" (total 20 grams).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The total cost of the journey for all the students must be 500 zeds or less.
There are 30 students in the class.

Here are the costs for visiting each town:

| Visiting Acton or Camford | Visiting Burley or Darley |
| --- | --- |
| Student Rate | Student Rate |
| Round-trip ticket: 25 zeds | Round-trip ticket: 20 zeds |
| 1/3 off for groups of 25 or more students | 10% off for groups of 15 or more students |

Which towns can they afford to visit? Show your work.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
